title: Open Personality Tests: OEJTS, OEPS, ODAT, IPIP-50, ECR-R
description: The five open personality tests behind AgentTune: what each measures, how it is scored, where ties happen, and how to run them in a browser or on an AI model.
h1: The five open personality tests, explained.
dek: What OEJTS, OEPS, ODAT, IPIP-50 and ECR-R measure, how they score, and where they break.
lede: This guide documents the five questionnaires used on AgentTune: their item sources, versioned scoring rules, tie handling, and practical limits. All five run locally in your browser at /tests/ with no signup, and each has a Markdown specification for reproducible scoring.
answer: AgentTune provides five browser-based questionnaire adaptations: OEJTS (32 items, MBTI-style), a 36-item OEPS adaptation (Enneagram), ODAT (16 items, DISC), IPIP-50 (50 items, Big Five) and ECR-R (36 items, attachment). All five score locally in your browser and preserve ties explicitly. Original AgentTune code and templates are MIT licensed; questionnaire items remain subject to their upstream source terms.

All five questionnaires run client-side in your browser and never upload your responses. Each test also has a machine-readable Markdown specification at /tests/<test>.md and a shared deterministic scorer at /resources/scoring/score.js. Review instrument-rights.json before redistributing third-party item text.

What it measures. Four preference axes: Extraversion vs. Introversion (E/I), Sensing vs. Intuition (S/N), Thinking vs. Feeling (T/F), and Judging vs. Perceiving (J/P). Each of the 32 items places two statements at opposite ends of a 1-to-5 scale, with eight items per axis.

Scoring. Each item contributes to its two poles so the axis sum is constant (48 across eight items, with 24 vs. 24 as an exact tie). Earlier reporting rules defaulted tied axes to I, N, T or J. The current quiz marks any tied axis as X, offers an optional tie-breaker preference, and only assigns a four-letter code when all four axes resolve.

Limits. OEJTS is an open scale that produces four-letter Jungian codes; it is not the trademarked MBTI® instrument. On short axes, a one-point difference flips the letter: in our September 2026 model dataset, GPT-6 Astra split 46 ISTJ to 45 INTJ with 29 runs tying on at least one axis, and Claude Opus 5.5 dropped from 94 legacy INTJ labels to 84 when ties were left open.

What it measures. Relative agreement across nine Enneagram types using a 36-item adaptation (four items per type, rated 1 to 5, no reverse-keyed items). The upstream live OEPS has 54 items.

Scoring. Sum the four items for each type (range 4 to 20). When one type has the unique highest total, its higher-scoring adjacent neighbor is reported as the wing (or no wing if the two adjacent types tie). When two or more types share the highest score, all tied leaders are reported together without forcing a winner.

Limits. Four items per type is a compact scale, so top-score ties are frequent: 40 to 65 of 100 runs tied at the top across all four fresh-session AI cohorts in September 2026. The open-source Enneagram scorer guide lets you inspect the exact tie arithmetic.

What it measures. Four workplace modes—Dominance (D), Influence (I), Steadiness (S), and Conscientiousness (C)—across 16 statements rated 1 to 5 (four items per dimension).

Scoring. Each dimension sums four items from 4 to 20. If one letter leads uniquely and the runner-up is within 2 points without a runner-up tie, the result is reported as a two-letter blend (such as SC or CS). Equal top totals remain an explicit tie rather than defaulting S ahead of C.

Limits. In our model evaluations, Dominance sits near the floor (4.0 to 6.0 out of 20) while Steadiness and Conscientiousness sit within a point or two of each other, producing top-score ties in 51 of 100 Fable runs and 39 of 100 Sol runs.

What it measures. Five continuous dimensions from Goldberg’s public-domain International Personality Item Pool markers: Openness (Intellect/Imagination), Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism (scored in the opposite direction of IPIP Emotional Stability). Fifty statements rated 1 (very inaccurate) to 5 (very accurate), 10 per trait, with 18 reverse-keyed items.

Scoring. Reverse-keyed items use 6 - response. Each dimension sums its 10 scored items (raw total 10 to 50; item mean 1.0 to 5.0). Missing or out-of-range answers return no final score.

Limits. Current results report raw totals and item averages without population percentiles or automatic template assignment. The earlier site’s heuristic reference centers had no verified normative sample. After reviewing your five scores, you can preview and combine any of the 10 high/low Big Five communication templates in the Big Five library or generator.

What it measures. Two adult attachment dimensions—attachment anxiety (items 1–18) and attachment avoidance (items 19–36)—rated 1 to 7, with 14 reverse-keyed items.

Scoring. Reverse-keyed items use 8 - response. Each axis is the mean of its 18 items (1.00 to 7.00). Using the scale midpoint of 4.00, scores map to four site categories: Secure (both ≤ 4), Anxious (anxiety > 4, avoidance ≤ 4), Avoidant (anxiety ≤ 4, avoidance > 4), and Disorganized (both > 4).

Limits. Because the statements describe close human relationships, administering them to a language model requires prompt translation, and small boundary shifts (such as Grok 4.6’s reported avoidance of 4.06 vs. a 4.00 cutoff) can flip a quadrant label.

sections.h2: Historical research provenance and direct preferences.
sections.html:
Published studies in the research hub used the frozen September 2026 and May 2026 adaptations. As documented in rights-migration.json, legacy MBTI item 1 and two legacy Enneagram items contained undocumented substitutions; raw response vectors and numeric summaries remain preserved for exact reproduction via the reproducibility guide.

Every questionnaire is optional. If you already know how you want your AI to respond, use the communication preferences builder or custom instructions generator directly.

faq.q: Are all five questionnaires MIT licensed?
faq.a: No. Original AgentTune software, scorers, and communication templates are MIT licensed, while questionnaire item text is governed by each source instrument’s terms (such as public-domain IPIP markers and Open Psychometrics / ECR-R source terms). Check instrument-rights.json before redistributing items.

faq.q: Does the Big Five test report population percentiles?
faq.a: No. It reports raw dimension totals (10 to 50) and item averages (1.0 to 5.0) so scores are transparent and never confused with a normed clinical percentile.

faq.q: Where do my answers go when I take a test?
faq.a: They stay in your browser tab. Scoring runs locally in JavaScript, and individual responses are never sent to an AgentTune server.

faq.q: Can an AI agent inspect the test specifications?
faq.a: Yes. Each questionnaire has a Markdown specification at /tests/<test>.md and is accessible via the get_test_spec tool on the AgentTune MCP server (https://agent-tune.com/mcp).
